thread:
incident-bot: Pager: High rate of GPU OOMs in us-west-2 decode-cluster (node group decode-prod-1). Affected service: /v1/streams (streaming decode). Error spike at 14:32 UTC. Auto-escalation to oncall.
maya (on-call): ack. I'm on it, checking dashboards now :eyes:
maya (on-call): metrics: 5xx for /v1/streams up from 0.4% -> 12% in last 5m. Pod restarts showing OOMKilled on g4dn nodes.
liam (runtime): saw this too — decode logs show repeated CUDA OOM during decode loop. stack trace: "CUDA: out of memory trying to allocate 512MB" then container killed.
rachel (sre): node flaps: 3 nodes reported kernel OOM events around same time, kube evicted pods. Possible runaway request(s) causing KV cache growth.
samir (product): any customer impact? which tenants hit?
maya (on-call): seeing elevated errors for tenant "acme-corp" (prod key), ~18% of requests dropped in that period. Not yet SLO breach but customer observed failures.
liam (runtime): quick root cause hypothesis: unbounded streaming generation from a background job — a missing/overriden max_tokens param caused continuous decode until EOS or explicit stop. Memory grows from KV cache + large attention buffers.
maya (on-call): can we temporarily block streaming endpoints for prod tenants? ops-bot, can we add a transient rule?
ops-bot: Adding rate-limit + hard max_tokens intercept at ingress for /v1/streams for prod tier. Patch applied: per-request token hard cap = 2048. (command: `kubectl apply -f ingress/temporary-stream-cap.yaml`)
liam (runtime): also killing long-lived decode sessions: `kubectl -n decode exec deploy/stream-gateway -- curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/admin/close-long-sessions` — closed ~120 sessions, freed ~80GB across cluster.
rachel (sre): rolling restart of affected node pool to recover kernel memory: `gcloud compute instances reset ...` scheduled, 2 nodes draining now.
samir (product): preparing customer comms: will notify ACME that we mitigated streaming failures, ETA for full fix?
liam (runtime): short-term: ingress cap + session kill + node restarts = stabilizing. Need code fix: ensure service validates client-specified max_tokens and enforce server-side upper bound and backpressure on streaming generators. Will cut a quick hotfix.
maya (on-call): handing off to liam for the next 2 hours. I'm switching to monitoring. If anything re-escalates, ping me.
liam (runtime): copying from local branch: `fix/stream-max-tokens-guard` — change in server: if `max_tokens == null || max_tokens > 10000` then reject with 400. config snippet:
```
# gateway config
stream: {
  max_tokens_server_cap: 10000,
  hard_reject_overflow: true
}
```
liam (runtime): deploying canary of hotfix to decode-staging, then to canary-prod with 5% traffic.
dev-rel-bot: automated smoke tests passed on canary (stream sanity), token enforcement appears to work.
ops-bot: canary rollout to 5% complete, monitoring for error spikes.
rachel (sre): metrics trending down. 5xx rate to 1.2% and falling. node flaps stopped.
incident-bot: Incident status -> Mitigated. Paging silenced. Retain this thread for postmortem notes.
samir (product): will open an incident ticket and coordinate postmortem. Requesting engineering change: server-side hard cap + alert for long-running stream sessions.
maya (on-call): Great work. I'll add runbook steps for future: 1) ingress hard cap, 2) session-kill endpoint, 3) node drain/reset. @liam please add tests for token limits.
liam (runtime): will do. creating PR and linking ticket: INC-4521.
rachel (sre): follow-up: recommend kernel oom tuning and pod memory requests review for decode nodes.
samir (product): I'll draft customer note and flag ACME's support ticket.
maya (on-call): Leaving notes here and closing my oncall shift. Handoff complete.
incident-bot: Incident status -> Resolved. Monitoring for 24h. Create postmortem in /ops/incidents/INC-4521 when ready.
